clue.text: An assortment taken from cloth pouch

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
a bag is a pouch or sack

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a mixed selection of items out of a cloth pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragbag is a jumbled collection of odds and ends, a motley assortment.

clue.text: A racket, commotion echoing in slaughterhouse

parts.note: a bat, as in table tennis, is a racket

indicators.note: an echo comes back, so the word for commotion is read in the return direction

parts.note: a riot is an uproar or commotion

explanation.surface: A noisy racket and commotion ring out inside a slaughterhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'echoing' signals a reversal because an echo sends sound back; 'racket' looks like noise, matching 'commotion', but here it is a sports bat.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a slaughterhouse, the French-derived word used in Britain.

clue.text: Old song, one rejecting love, by Danielle, possibly

indicators.note: possibly tells us the letters may be rearranged into another word
one rejecting love means the word one throws out its letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone who has spurned love is linked to a woman called Danielle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' drops O from ONE, leaving NE; 'possibly' then rearranges NE with DANIELLE. 'Nellie Dean' is an old British music-hall song, a pub singalong favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Nellie Dean is a sentimental Edwardian music-hall song, so it is an old song by name.

clue.text: Another identical cooking range at home

parts.note: identical means the same
an Aga is a well-known British brand of range cooker
someone at home is said to be in

explanation.surface: Someone orders a second, identical cooking range for the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Same again' is what a pub customer says when ordering another round of the same drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for the same again in a bar means asking for another of the same drink.

clue.text: Blackleg locked in pickets' cabin

indicators.note: locked in says the answer is shut inside the following words

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker is shut inside the picketers' hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackleg is a worker who crosses a picket line, which is also called a scab.

clue.text: Servant shuffling in, lame

indicators.note: shuffling mixes things up, so the next letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lame servant shuffles into the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a domestic servant or one doing lowly work.

clue.text: Deduction in wages resulting from industrial action?

definitions.meaning: a sum stopped, that is held back, from pay
a strike, when workers stop work

explanation.surface: Workers lose pay because of a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is both money withheld from wages and a halt to work in a dispute.

clue.text: Going round in the morning, criminal pinches one

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks a time in the morning

indicators.note: pinches means grips, so the word for criminal holds the letter for one

parts.note: bent is slang for corrupt or criminal
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A crook does the rounds early in the day, stealing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinches' suggests stealing, but here it means gripping: BENT holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient means surrounding or encompassing, so it is going round something.

clue.text: Vehicle clipped vagrant

indicators.note: clipped means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: a tramp is a vagrant

explanation.surface: A vehicle knocks over a homeless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' looks like a collision but cuts the last letter, P, from TRAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a vehicle running on rails along streets.

clue.text: Very old worker drinking nice bubbly

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the word for worker swallows the rest

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and effervescence, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: An elderly employee is sipping some pleasant champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like a noun for champagne, the drink the worker sips, but it is the anagram signal; 'drinking' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient is a synonym for very old.

clue.text: Fight and cut domineering woman

parts.note: a battle is a fight
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A forceful woman is told to fight and slash.
explanation.definitionFit: Battleaxe is an informal term for an aggressive, domineering woman.

clue.text: Colonel's uninspiring after lead of brigadier

indicators.note: after puts the word for uninspiring behind the first piece
the lead of a word is its front, its first letter

parts.note: limp means feeble, lacking vigour

explanation.surface: An army colonel proves dull when compared with his brigadier.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp is a cartoon figure of a pompous, reactionary British officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Blimp, David Low's cartoon character, gave the name for a blustering old officer.

clue.text: Item of wear girl's beginning to be very fond of

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: to love is to be very fond of

explanation.surface: A girl starts to really like a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove is an item worn on the hand.

clue.text: Something of a thug, or, I'll add, an ape

indicators.note: Something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone adds that a thuggish brute is rather like an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in thuG and continues through OR and ILL to the A of add.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is the largest of the great apes.

clue.text: Spanish footballers, very angry, clear

parts.note: real is informal for very, as in real good
mad means angry
to rid is to clear

explanation.surface: Spanish players are told, furiously, to get off the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Real Madrid is a famous Spanish football club, so its players are Spanish footballers.

clue.text: Student nun organised hop inside

indicators.note: inside places the rearranged letters within the word for nun

parts.note: a nun is called Sister

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A student nun arranges a dance in the convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' is the anagram signal and 'inside' the container signal; 'hop' looks like a dance but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophister is a second- or third-year undergraduate, especially at Trinity College Dublin.

clue.text: Amicably drop unresolved argument? Regret idea, as ego affected

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of these words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone regrets an idea because their pride was wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges the letters of REGRET IDEA AS EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to disagree is to end a dispute politely while each side keeps its view.

clue.text: County youth held by expert gives tribute

indicators.note: held by means the following pieces sit inside the word for expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A skilled local player pays homage to a young county cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise, a tribute.

clue.text: Continual red tape, ridiculous when Ecstasy's involved

indicators.note: involved means drawn in, so the letter for the drug is put inside
ridiculous means absurd, so the letters of these words are scrambled

parts.note: E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Endless bureaucracy becomes absurd once drugs are involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' rearranges RED TAPE into REPATED, and 'involved' takes E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated, happening again and again, can mean continual.

clue.text: Ancient Greek city, in North, I suspect, by Cape

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that an ancient Greek city lies in the north beside a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' is the anagram signal; 'in' and 'by' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth was a major city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Take away produce

definitions.meaning: to take away is to ... something
to produce is to bring out, as a wallet from a pocket

explanation.definitionFit: Remove means take away, and to remove something from a pocket is to produce it.

clue.text: Bike was blue

explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a light motorbike, and moped is also the past tense of mope, to be gloomy.

clue.text: Dictator in terminal receiving head of state

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the word for terminal gets the letter inside

parts.note: a depot is a bus or train terminal

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dictator in a station terminal greets a visiting leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a tyrant or dictator who rules absolutely.

clue.text: Crash — female cut

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A woman is injured in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a failure, as is a crash in business.

clue.text: I'm entering illuminated border

indicators.note: entering means going into, so these letters go inside the word for illuminated

parts.note: lit means illuminated
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they are walking into a brightly lit frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or border.

clue.text: Go for a short walk

definitions.meaning: a go is one's chance to play, as in whose go is it
a ... is a brief stroll, as in a ... around the garden

explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a go in a game, and taking a turn in the park is a short stroll.

clue.text: Speaks about a son and daughter making a musical

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for speaks surrounds the rest

parts.note: says means speaks
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone describes how their son and daughter put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Salad Days is a long-running 1950s British stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad Days is the title of a well-known British musical by Julian Slade.

clue.text: Various aquatic birds by far edge of lake

parts.note: divers are water birds, the British name for loons

indicators.note: far edge of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Various water birds gather beside the far side of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse means varied or of several kinds, so various.

clue.text: Old card game shown in book in front of Oscar

indicators.note: in front of places the word for book before the next letter

parts.note: a primer is an elementary schoolbook
Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: An old card game appears in a book about the Academy Awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Primero is a sixteenth-century gambling card game, an ancestor of poker.
